identity.deal: Kill Tony regular who turns the immigrant-son lens on American absurdity with clean setups and a quiet kill.
identity.premise: A man who treats the American way of life as a strange customs office and files the paperwork out loud.
identity.awareness_note: Semi: the outsider lens is the act; the craft is getting tighter.

philosophy.ontology: America is a series of rituals nobody explains to newcomers.
philosophy.epistemology: If you describe the ritual precisely, the absurdity appears.
philosophy.axiology: The outsider sees the room better than the room sees itself.
philosophy.causality: One precise observation about a custom becomes a whole worldview.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be foreign; almost nobody uses it as a scalpel.

dramatic_core.want: to name the ritual nobody names
dramatic_core.fear: becoming part of the ritual and losing the lens
dramatic_core.need: the room to see itself through his eyes
dramatic_core.self_model: a man holding a clipboard at the door of American life
blind_spots: the outsider lens can thin out

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats American customs as alien ceremonies and describes them with the precision of an ethnographer who's also a little offended.
contradictions: the outsider who became an insider
the clean setup with the dark turn
the regular who grew into the stage

status_model.felt_status: a man permanently at the door of the room

essay_seeds.title: Hans Kim: 'America as a strange customs office' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: Describes a normal American ritual with the precision of someone who wasn't raised in it. literalize: treats the ritual as if it were literally as strange as it sounds when described fresh. The room recognizes the absurdity they'd stopped seeing.

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
